title: Exploration of patient risk profiles for adverse drug reactions – Establishment of a care cohort of patients under complex drug therapies
summary:
Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are a common reason for medical consultations, particularly in emergency departments and among older adults. Approximately 6.5% of emergency department visits and 8.7% of hospital admissions in this age group are attributed to ADRs. Since 80–90% of ADRs are dose-dependent, it is crucial to understand the factors that increase the risk.
This study aims to identify patients at higher risk for ADRs who may benefit from specialized medication counseling. It examines genetic factors that influence how the body metabolizes drugs, as well as interactions between different medications. Additionally, the study assesses how well individual drug metabolism can be predicted by measuring known or less-researched metabolic products.
The study relies exclusively on data from routine medical treatment and supplements these, when possible, with blood and potentially urine samples. During a (video) consultation, information about previous medication use and common side effects is collected. An interdisciplinary case conference then evaluates how likely the reported symptoms are caused by medications (following WHO standards) and how they impact the patient’s quality of life.
For patients who have undergone whole genome sequencing as part of genetic diagnostics (e.g., for investigating a rare genetic disorder) or who have received at least one specific pharmacogenetic test, data on pharmacogenetically relevant variants should be used for research purposes.

interventions.name: Patients eligible for clinical pharmacological therapy consultation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Treatment involves a specialized, complex drug therapy as determined by a specialist, requiring individualized clinical pharmacological consultation
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to consent
